title: Remove the cold source-stage native preparation bottleneck
description: Complete native source-stage requests miss the cold C frontend gate even though the prepared RMD frontend passes all three final workloads. Final medians (prepared / full inline request / original-C GCC syntax): intrusive1.778/11.274/6.907ms; 1k13.478/23.484/18.445ms; 8k109.505/123.053/111.167ms. Final target GCC parsing, compilation, and linking are excluded by user instruction. Host setup attribution: BFD link7.33ms, as1.53ms; installed gold/LLD alternatives also miss. A bounded checked one-call libffi proof passes output/ownership and measures2.046ms versus GCC6.700ms but is not a general evaluator. Before replacing execution, establish complete expressions/control flow, aggregate local storage, native callbacks, reentrancy, scalar ABI, and loaded-code lifetime; do not add partial execution or silent fallback. Prepared-code reuse is another path: key actual host source and native inputs, compiler/profile/options, keep target snapshots valid, execute build once per request, and never replay or skip effects without a declared contract. Preserve the actual intrusive witness, arbitrary ordinary host RMD semantics, no compiler dependencies in targets, and separate host preparation from target frontend timing.
notes: The source-order investigation is in docs/source-order-compilation.md. The requested entry is rmd main.rmd, with executed root actions controlling stages and target files. Whole-root native preparation cannot implement unread-root reader replacement. Before a complete executor, prove one bounded reader transfer through real intrusive target output with retained source, callback, and module lifetimes. Current token lookahead crosses action boundaries; repeated collect/resolve over an expanding context is quadratic. Keep each action with its matching executor and preserve stable declaration identities across contexts. This research ran no new compiler timing and changed no production compiler code.
close_reason: Removed implicit native root preparation. The complete source-order path passes all three final 25-pair gates through full C and rename output: intrusive 2.461 ms, 1k 14.018 ms, 8k 109.335 ms; each root/GCC 95% upper bound is below 1.0. Preserved failed baseline, controlled profiles, rejected candidates, and separately measured explicit native-library preparation. Final target GCC remains excluded.

title: Add a C backend written in RMD0 as a compiled metastage
description: Implement the complete C-emitting backend in ordinary RMD0 without C lowering, formatting, or backend helper bridges. Consume exposed checked trees; retain the C bootstrap frontend and host allocation/IO boundary. Compile generated C with system GCC. Prove direct intrusive-list reclamation, exact seed semantics and native ABI under optimization, and self-translation of the stage before expansion. Measure stage compilation cost separately from GCC. Document and commit.
close_reason: Implemented the complete C backend and driver in RMD0; self-compilation and intrusive reuse passed. Final seed suite passed 10896 C API and 398 integration checks; C backend passed 348 checks at O2 and with an instrumented O3 stage and programs. Final 25-round complete-output speed gate passed; documented source-matched results.

description: Compare current official Zig documentation and public Jai creator and source evidence before adding source syntax. Record compile-time execution, build control, parser boundaries, phase ownership, parallel work, cache limits, and the effect on the proposed file envelope. Keep the source-directed backend implementation task open until its ownership and cost witnesses pass.
close_reason: Rechecked official Zig 0.16 and 0.17 development material, public Jai creator evidence and concrete same-file examples with two research agents. Recorded source-defined stage requirements, rejected mandatory meta/payload framing for backend selection, preserved reader/checker/module/backend replacement and full cold-cost gates, and checked the document with both agents. No syntax added.

title: Investigate source-order execution and replaceable interpretation
description: Compare the current leading meta block with a small source-order controller: read one complete host action, execute it, and let that action change the reader and stages for unread source. Check Python, Forth, Lisp/Scheme/Racket and academic precedents from primary sources. Define bootstrap rules, lookahead and cursor ownership, host versus target meaning, forward references, phase publication, concurrency, effect replay, and caching. Keep target GCC compilation and linking outside frontend measurements. Write a reviewable design proposal and bounded experiment; do not change language syntax or production compiler during investigation. Preserve current spec and implementation until a replacement is reviewed.
close_reason: Completed source-checked research with three subagents. Added docs/source-order-compilation.md, retained the implemented specification, and recorded a repeatable 9/9 Python boundary witness. Defined root CLI, source-order reader and execution boundaries, target separation, lifetime, concurrency, effects, cache requirements, current parser/checker failure mechanisms, and a bounded output and speed experiment. Production compiler syntax is unchanged.

title: Use Linux, GCC, and LLVM source patterns as language capability requirements
description: Inspect pinned Linux, GCC, LLVM, and Code of Honor source for intrusive lists, graph mutation, ownership, concurrency, callbacks, and layout. Record concrete capability witnesses. Replace the mandatory checked-pool direction with direct embedded links and explicit lifetime contracts, per user correction. Preserve the requirement for user-written list code without unsafe and C-level frontend speed; do not claim unproved memory safety. Use subagents for source research and design review.
close_reason: Inspected pinned Linux, GCC, LLVM, and Coho sources with subagents. Added source witnesses and revised the proposal around direct embedded links, independent ownership, and explicit lifetime requirements. Removed the mandatory pool direction. Verified document links and source ranges; safety and compilation-speed gates remain stated as unproved experiments.

title: Specify the minimal extensible bootstrap language
description: Reread the complete research corpus and define a closed minimal language specification with grammar, static and execution rules, modules, memory and foreign boundaries, and public compiler-stage composition. Put complex ownership, unsafe policy, and backends in compiled language libraries. Preserve C-speed gates and unresolved standard-language requirements without adding speculative features. Cross-review with three agents and commit the reviewed specification.
close_reason: Completed the minimal RMD0 specification and public stage contracts. Module management is a library stage. Three agent reviews resolved grammar, memory, ABI, and staging findings. The grammar audit passed 102 observations, all 80 local documentation links passed, and diff checks passed. Research and measured performance evidence are preserved without claiming an implemented compiler or solved checked-list rule.

description: Investigate public Jai metacompilation, Lisp and Scheme/Racket, Forth and Factor, academic staging and extensible compiler work, and cache and parallel scheduling costs. title: Implement source-order compilation from the root program
description: Implement rmd main.rmd per docs/source-order-compilation.md. Then add a minimal checked-AST execution mechanism, exact action reader and incremental host checking, ordinary library stage/file control, full host semantics and native callbacks. Validate source-order effects, hostile-byte syntax switching, root arguments and status, target artifacts, source diagnostics, and cold frontend cost.

Strict suites pass: 21904 unit checks, 398 x64, 348 C, 141 root process checks. GCC ASan/UBSan validates the root and C backend. title: Implement the RMD0 bootstrap compiler in pedantic C99
description: Implement the specified raw RMD0 language in pedantic C99 with arena allocation, explicit compiler contexts, public stage APIs, and a textual x86-64 System V adapter. GCC assembles and links its output. Establish an executable intrusive-list witness and frontend timing baseline before expansion. Validate syntax, types, evaluation, memory/layout, traps, scalar ABI, error paths, RMD0-compiled stage replacement, and parallel isolation. Keep module and ownership policy outside the core. Document measured results and commit.
close_reason: Implemented the complete RMD0 seed in 4813 C/header lines with arena allocation, public stages, GNU x86-64 assembly, direct intrusive lists, and a compiled replacement stage. Strict GCC and Clang, ASAN/UBSAN, and TSAN pass. All nine paired timing gates pass; complete 8k assembly median110.588ms vs GCC syntax115.064ms, ratio CI0.955-0.968. Source and exact failed-baseline reconstruction recorded.

Count inline native preparation and changed project-library preparation against paired C baselines; current BFD attribution identifies native linking as the small-input speed-gate failure. Validate a bounded remedy before expanding architecture. Test, document, sync, and commit.
notes: Git metadata is writable again. Implementation and recorded validation were checked before staging. Cold host preparation performance remains separately tracked.
